fields.notes: The TFP410 datasheet documents NO confidentiality, integrity-against-tampering, or authentication features. The TMDS encoding provides no cryptographic protection. HDCP cipher and key storage live in a separate licensed device. CEC (Consumer Electronics Control) — HDMI 1-wire bidirectional remote-control bus — is also OUTSIDE TFP410 scope. For production DVI/HDMI sources requiring HDCP / CEC, integrate TFP410 with a separate HDCP cipher chip and CEC controller.
anti_corruption_mechanisms: TMDS 8 → 10b transition-minimised encoding — designed for transition minimisation + DC balance, NOT for integrity or authentication.
Running disparity tracking per channel — prevents long DC drift.
Control character codes — high transition density.
DDC EDID checksum (byte 127) — validates EDID transport, not a security feature.
I2C ACK / NAK — standard bus-level integrity.
HPD presence — receiver indicator (no cryptographic guarantee).

hdcp_status.hdcp_transport_via_DDC: Possible — TFP410's I2C bridge can carry HDCP traffic to/from receiver at 0x74/0x75.

fields.ctl3_hdcp_reservation: CTL[3] is reserved for HDCP and is always encoded as 0 by TFP410.
